data.what: Resolved a pending config/symbol request whose session ended as status='all_rejected' with response left NULL, rather than adding a 'session_ended' value to the setting_change_request enum. The plan offered either.
data.why: main-prod deploys code BEFORE schema (blue-green flips the image, then the rail migrates), so new code writing an enum value the DB does not yet carry fails for the whole window between the two — and a rollback re-serves an image that would keep failing. all_rejected is truthful (nothing was applied) and a robot ack ALWAYS writes response, so 'all_rejected AND response IS NULL' is an unambiguous discriminator that costs no schema change.
data.costIfWrong: P10 (stale-robot banner / 'no answer yet') and P26 must key on the PAIR, not on a single status word; a consumer that reads only status cannot tell a robot's rejection from a session-end retirement.

data.what: heartbeat_interval_seconds on GET /{role}/sessions/{id} is read from a Valkey key the heartbeat republishes (config:robot:heartbeat-interval-seconds, TTL 900s), not from SSM as the plan's parenthetical said.
data.why: session-manager has neither the SSM SDK nor a PARAMETER_PREFIX env key. Adding them means a lambdas.yaml environment entry + an IAM statement + a hetzner env-manifest baseline bump — a registered cutover-class change and a parity:env break — for one advisory integer, in a phase whose stated property is 'task aws:plan stays zero-change'. Both lambdas already carry the cache-utilities layer, the SSM parameter remains the SSOT, and the fallback is the SAME compiled-in 60 the heartbeat uses, so nothing can drift.
data.costIfWrong: For the first ~5 minutes after a deploy (before any robot heartbeat refreshes the key) the session read serves the default 60 rather than a customised SSM value. If an operator ever needs it exact-on-first-read, wire PARAMETER_PREFIX into session-manager as a registered change.

data.what: An explicitly EMPTY changeable_config_keys reads as UNDECLARED (permissive), not as 'no key is changeable'.
data.why: trade emits changeable_config_keys: [] whenever nothing is changeable (RobotDeclarations.allows_config_changes is bool(keys)) and the bridge derives supports_config_changes from the same fact, so [] beside a true flag is a contradictory pair — and supports_config_changes, which the Postgres trigger has always enforced, is the honest gate for it. Mirrors parseSymbolScope, which reads an allowlist with no usable symbol as undeclared.
data.costIfWrong: A product that declares [] while claiming supports_config_changes=true would accept config changes its binary refuses — the pre-P25 behaviour, i.e. no regression, only a missed tightening.

Six BL rows closed plus the platform half of a seventh: - **🔴 BL-45 (security)** — a change-request ack was resolved by `request_id` **alone**. data.what: The module tier surfaced that P25's EXPAND migration 2026-09-06-01 can NEVER auto-apply: it is ordered AFTER the contract-phase boundary 2026-08-14-01-rls-app-rt-nobypassrls.sql, so db-migrate.sh holds it and every other file behind it. Recorded as a P14 blocker rather than fixed here.
data.why: Fixing it means renaming/re-dating a migration file, which is aws-scope schema work and belongs to the phase that ships it (P14), not to a phase whose job is to build a test tier. And the fix is not obviously a rename: SCHEMA_GATE_ACK removes the boundary ENTIRELY rather than narrowing to one file, so P14 will apply FIVE pending files (2026-09-01-01, 2026-09-01-02, 2026-09-03-01, 2026-09-06-01 and the gated 2026-08-14-01 itself), not one -- which is a decision about production, not a tidy-up. P22's own exit criterion (3) is satisfied regardless: db-init.sh bakes the current schema, so runtime.sessions.last_heartbeat_at exists on the dev db and the tier proves the column end to end.
data.costIfWrong: If P14 assumes its single EXPAND file will auto-apply, db:migrate:status will show it still pending after the ship and the exit criterion fails at the worst moment -- mid-deploy, on the production box.

data.what: Did NOT squash-merge aws PR #176, though the gate's conditions for it are met

Squashing first would deadlock the two plans against each other. Measured: with #104's two entries present, the lint against aws origin/main (0976f442) is exit 0.
data.costIfWrong: If #104 never merges, aws #176 sits open; nothing is lost. If I had squashed first, #104 goes red and both ship lanes stall until someone reconciles the register by hand.

data.what: The KEK refusal is APPLY-only: --apply exits 2 without a usable KEK, --dry-run warns on stderr and still reports its counts.
data.why: The plan says 'refuses without a KEK' AND lists a bare '.venv/bin/python scripts/backfill_license_secrets.py --dry-run' in §Verification. Both cannot hold: no dev box here has a rendered KEK, so a blanket refusal makes the plan's own verification line exit 2. --apply is the only mode that writes, and the only place store_secret's non-production plaintext fallback could turn a backfill into a no-op reported as success; a dry run writes nothing, so refusing there protects nothing and blocks the command an operator runs first to size the job.
data.costIfWrong: If P13 expected a dry-run to be a KEK readiness probe, it must now read the stderr WARNING (or run --apply) rather than the exit code. The handoff states this.

data.what: Committed to MQL52026 (compile-service/config/pins/MANIFEST.md, 73edf08, draft PR #100) even though P6's declared Repos are trade/acme-backend,hub.
data.why: MIRROR_SOURCES is deliberately ONE roster so a mirror pair cannot be added on one side only, and test_the_manifest_lists_every_mirror_pair enforces it. Adding verify_checks.json on the tb side alone leaves the manifest — which hub's task drift:pins reads — naming three pairs while four are compared. No MQL52026 lock was held (conflicts clear). Committing to the run branch is not deploying; only a merge ships box #3, and the PR is a draft for a ship phase to take.
data.costIfWrong: If tb PR #105 merges before MQL52026 #100, anyone holding both checkouts on main gets a red test_the_manifest_lists_every_mirror_pair. tb CI cannot catch it (the test skips with no MQL52026 checkout), so the ordering is stated in #100's body and in the handoff.

data.what: Repaired an INHERITED red: added .gitleaksignore with 6 line-anchored fingerprints for P2's hmac_vectors.json placeholder.
data.why: secret-scan ran on this branch for the first time on P6's push and failed on six matches introduced by 9b1ea4e8 (P2). quality.yml now CALLS the scanners, so they bind required-checks and the branch cannot merge red — a phase that leaves its own PR unmergeable has not finished. P5 fingerprinted the byte-identical MQL52026 copy the same way.
data.costIfWrong: If the intent was ever to rewrite the fixture rather than fingerprint it, this entrenches the placeholder. It cannot be rewritten cheaply: the vectors are derived from it and the file is byte-compared across repos, so changing it needs an MQL52026 ship.

data.what: Asserted VERIFY_TIERS against the tiers the roster declares checks for, not against MT-CVS's PLATFORM_COVERAGE.
data.why: The plan says 'verify_tiers asserted equal to the roster's coverage', but PLATFORM_COVERAGE (mt5 A,B,C,D / mt4 B) is a Python constant in MQL52026's app/verify/models.py and is NOT a field of verify_checks.json, so it does not travel in the mirror. Publishing it into the roster is an MQL52026 generator change. Equality is also wrong on its face: mt5 asks CVS for B,C,D while coverage says A,B,C,D, because tier A is the aws worker's embed.
data.costIfWrong: A tier tb asks for that the roster has no check for is caught; a PLATFORM-specific mismatch (tb asking mt4 for tier D) is not. Recorded in the handoff as a follow-up needing an MQL52026 roster field.

data.what: On an invalid_status refusal the heartbeat's change-ack outcome echoes the status the ROBOT sent, which is by construction outside that field's own three-verdict enum. Documented the exception in session-global.yaml rather than fabricating a verdict or dropping the field.
data.why: The alternative readings were: coerce to all_rejected (states the robot reported something it did not), or omit status (breaks the field's required-ness for every other outcome). Echoing the truth and telling clients to read rejected_reason first is the only option that keeps the response honest; a robot that sent an illegal status is already off-contract.
data.costIfWrong: A strict generated client that validates status before rejected_reason could throw on this one refusal path instead of surfacing it. Only reachable by a robot that already sent an illegal status.

data.what: Adjudicated the 18 by a single rule: adopt a recorded fixture ONLY where the recording actually exercises the behaviour the fixture is named for; where it does not, keep the hand-written specimen and file the capture gap as a finding.
data.why: Three of the 16 recordings do not correspond to their cell: the three mt4 robot 'live' journals are a 3-line MT4 terminal boot banner (MT4 writes the EA journal to MQL4/Logs, the capture read Logs/), indicator_mt5.journal.txt is a FAILED probe run (OnInit critical error 4002) while the ring graded I-ON-S pass, and the indicator reject/expired journals log 'key=absent' so no rejection ever occurs. Adopting them would have made the suite assert that mt4 fails every tier-D check and that the tier-C probe produces no verdict — deleting exactly the coverage the corpus was meant to make real.
data.costIfWrong: If these recordings are in fact faithful, four fixtures stay hand-written for one more phase and the findings are re-litigated; nothing ships wrong. The reverse error is silent and permanent.

data.what: The scrubber JSON-secret fix was NEVER on acme-backend main; this phase re-lands it in the corpus PR instead of treating it as already shipped.
data.why: The P18 handoff recorded tb #114 -> 04d685ed as 'the recorder text guard + the scrubber JSON-secret fix', and box #2 deployed it green. Both halves of that are false about the scrubber: PR #114's head was 08e63f8b (record_journals.py ONLY), 485f3df8 was committed after the PR existed and never pushed to it, and the squash BODY describes the scrubber fix while its diff does not contain it. origin/main's _SECRET_ASSIGN_RE still lacks the jwt keyword and the closing-quote separator, so anyone running task e2e:record from main today would write live api_keys and session JWTs into the corpus again — the exact 25-finding failure the fix was written for.
data.costIfWrong: None: re-landing a patch already present is a no-op diff. Not landing it leaves a security-relevant fix that every provenance record claims exists.

data.why: the plan's row\.secret also matches row.secret_encrypted, so it false-reds on CORRECT code (store_secret's sealed write); the tightened regex is clean on #117 and still matches all 3 read paths in the old image

data.what: The apply verb is task hetzner:backup then task prod:migrate:head on the box, NOT task hetzner:update:db
data.why: hetzner:update:db runs prod:migrate, which migrates only to alembic_contract_gate --auto-target and can never apply a held contract phase
data.costIfWrong: none — measured from Taskfile.yml prod:migrate / prod:migrate:head

data.what: alembic_contract_gate learned migrations/contract-phase-applied.txt and a 32-char revision-id guard (in #118)
data.why: p86 is trade's FIRST real contract phase; a probe proved alembic treats upgrade <ancestor> as a silent no-op, so after the hand-apply every later expand revision would be held forever. And p86's first draft id (41 chars) overflowed alembic_version VARCHAR(32) — caught by the snapshot regen, would have failed the production apply
data.costIfWrong: a later session forgets to record an apply; the registry refuses unknown or non-contract ids

data.what: #118 keeps #117's declared-but-unmapped column in the model; the model sheds it in the post-apply follow-up PR
data.why: CI's schema-contract job migrates to --auto-target (p85) and runs the autogen ratchet against the MODEL: a column-less model read as NEW divergence remove_column:compile_licenses.secret on #118's first push
data.costIfWrong: one more small tb PR after the apply

data.what: p72's expression index on params_snapshot->license->license_id is now read by nothing
data.why: its only reader was the verdict route's legacy scan, removed in #117; dropping an index is a separate migration and was not in P20's scope
data.costIfWrong: a small unused index keeps costing writes to indicator_compile_run

data.what: Dev stacks now need AI_BUILDER_KEK to mint licensed compiles (seal-or-refuse everywhere); the laptop's dev .env has none
data.why: the plaintext fallback that let a KEK-less dev box mint went with the column; .env.example documents it and the suite carries a fake KEK. Editing the shared gitignored dev .env was not asked for
